tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

setup-components: Introduction, p.5: the authors list the setup components in one sentence, read in context with the scene description.
scene-wall-obscurant: Introduction, p.5: the 2-inch metallic diffuser wall and the aluminum mesh obscurant are stated as the experimental scene.
upconversion-three-conditions: Methods, p.17: the authors state the three conditions for up-conversion in the NGSPD they built. It is the operating condition of their own detector, not a measured result.
pulse-parameters: Methods, p.16: 6.6 ps FWHM pump at 1565.5 nm, 6.1 ps probe, 50 MHz mode-locked laser, all stated as apparatus parameters. The probe wavelength in the text reads '1545.1 ps' (a typo) and the value correctly omits it.
probe-energy-beam: Methods, p.16: EDFA amplification to about 0.2 nJ per pulse and a 2.2 mm Gaussian collimated beam are stated apparatus parameters.
geometry-90cm-20deg: Methods, p.17: 90 cm MEMS-to-diffuser distance and 20 degree tilt (MEMS at rest) stated verbatim as geometry.
circulator-isolation: Methods, p.17: fiber circulator with minimum isolation ratio 55 dB and temporal separation by narrow optical gating are stated as design of the apparatus.
detector-spec: Methods, p.17: PPLN waveguide module, silicon SPAD about 70% at 780 nm, center phase-matching wavelength 1559.8 nm, stated in the detector description.
scan-32x32-acq-time: NLOS imaging section, p.6 and p.9: 32x32 raster scan with photon count versus pump delay, and the acquisition protocol (about 15 min at 10 ms dwell per delay point) are stated as protocol, not as a performance result.
denoise-l1-method: NLOS imaging section, p.7, Eq. 1: per-point l1-regularized convex filtering with CVX, lambda 0.1, then light-cone reconstruction. This is the paper's stated computational procedure.
positioning-method: Position retrieval section, p.11-12: least-sum-square matching of first-photon arrival times with a Gaussian joint probability and sigma_t approximated as FWHM/2 = 5 ps. It is the paper's own method description.
vibrometry-method: Acousto-optics sensing section, p.12-13: FPGA photon-count sampling at 1 kHz followed by a short-time Fourier transform is stated as the sensing protocol.
limit-acquisition-depth: Discussion, p.14: 'One major drawback of the current NGSPD approach' is the pump-delay scan, which makes acquisition slow and limits imaging depth. The authors state it about their own system.
circuit-model-resource: Section 2, p.4: the author defines the circuit model by its resource, the number of 1- and 2-qubit gates, and says this is what matters in practice. This is how the paper frames the model.
black-box-model-definition: Section 2, p.4: the black-box (oracle, query) model is defined by its resource (queries to a black box that reversibly computes f, callable on superpositions) and by the rule that f is learned only through calls.
yz-task-definition: Section 4, p.6: the author defines the Yamakawa-Zhandry task in his own words (random or pseudorandom f, n strings each mapped to 0, concatenation an n^2-bit codeword of a stated code). Value matches the passage, including the n^2 rendering. The task itself comes from reference [44].
forrelation-definition: Section 6, p.9: Forrelation is defined as deciding whether g is close to the Boolean Fourier transform of f or independent of f, under a promise. Value matches.
collision-problem-definition: Section 7, p.11: the collision problem is defined for a 2-to-1 function f from {1..N} to {1..M}, M >= N, finding x,y with f(x)=f(y). Value matches.
abbas-definition-effective-dimension: Section 3.2, Definition 3.1, Eq. 2: the effective dimension is defined with gamma and n via the normalised Fisher matrix. The text says the two differences from the definition in [20] (gamma and the log n term) help in proving the bound.
abbas-theorem-3-2-statement: Section 3.3, Theorem 3.2, Eq. 5; proof in Appendix B.1 via Lemma B.1, Lemma B.2 (union bound plus Hoeffding) and a final substitution. The value carries the conditions: Lipschitz (4), full-rank Fisher matrix, bounded log-gradient Lambda, bounded alpha-Holder loss.
abbas-lemma-b1-covering-number: Appendix B.1, Lemma B.1: stated with its conditions and proved in the appendix. The proof says it follows [20] and then carries out the determinant and covering argument in full (Eq. 6, operator monotonicity of the determinant).
abbas-lemma-b2-uniform-deviation: Appendix B.1, Lemma B.2: stated with its conditions and proved in the appendix (Holder continuity, union bound over covering balls, Hoeffding, Eqs. 7-10). It generalises a textbook result but the argument is written out.
abbas-remark-3-3-limit-maximal-rank: Remark 3.3 and Appendix B.3: the proof that d_gamma,n tends to the maximal Fisher rank has both directions written out (upper bound by diagonalising and bounding, lower bound on the set A of maximal rank). The non-monotonicity in n is explained by an example in B.4 and the sufficiently-large-n caveat in footnote 12.
abbas-theorem-b5-discretised-bound: Appendix B.5, Theorem B.5 with Lemma B.6 and proof, p.17-19: stated with conditions and proved, for the discretised model only. Remark B.7 gives approximation conditions as discussion, and the value says so. Eq. 13 uses 4B^2 where Lemma B.2 has 2B^2, a minor inconsistency.
abbas-model-setup-feature-map-and-variat: Section 2 and Appendix A.1-A.2: Hadamard layer, RZ and RZZ encoding repeated once (feature-map depth 2), RY plus CNOT variational form, z-basis parity readout, d = (D+1)S parameters, and the easy model as the first Hadamard and RZ layer only. All stated as the paper's models.
abbas-feature-map-hardness-conjectured: Section 2 text and footnotes 2 and 4, p.2-3: the authors say the feature map is 'believed' hard to simulate classically (motivated in [39]) and 'conjectured' hard for depth >= 2, and that easy/hard mean classical simulability of the encoding. The paper itself marks classical hardness as unproved.
abbas-comparable-models-definition: Section 2 footnotes 1 and 5, Section 4: comparable means same parameter count, input size and output size. The classical set uses feedforward networks with all topologies, with and without biases, RELU, leaky RELU, tanh, sigmoid. The study covers d <= 100, s_in in {4,6,8,10}, s_out = 2. All stated as protocol.
abbas-parameter-space-convention-limit: Appendix C.3, footnote 28, p.20: [-1,1]^d is used for initialisation and for the effective dimension for consistency with classical literature, and the authors note that using either parameter space does affect the observed effective-dimension results. A caveat on their own results.
abbas-effective-dimension-generalisation: Theorem 3.2 states the stored conditions and also the log-Fisher gradient bound and a bounded loss, and is proved in Appendix B.1. Remark 3.4 and Theorem B.5 give the discretised version. The new value matches the passage and is proved here.
qensemble-described: Introduction, p.1: the paper describes the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers as parallel evaluation, weighing by a scheme, and single-qubit readout. It matches the formal definition in the Review section (Eqs. 3-4).
scope-two-results: Introduction, p.1-2: the authors state what the paper covers, the accuracy-weighted scheme dequantised and the general framework shown to contain Deutsch-Jozsa. Only the coverage is settled here. The strength of the two results is not (see the dequantisation items).
ensemble-prediction-def: Review section, Eq. 2, p.1: the ensemble prediction is the sign of the weighted sum of model outputs, with weights w_theta. Value matches.
qensemble-routines-w-a: Review section, Eqs. 3-4, p.2: routine W sets the weights, routine A computes f, and together they form the quantum ensemble. Value matches.
qensemble-class-prob: Review section, p.2: probability of measuring the last qubit in |0> is the prediction -1, and the class probabilities are weight sums over the model subsets E+/-, normalised. Value is worded loosely enough to match. Note the paper pairs p(-1) with E+ although it defines E+/- by predictions +/-1, which looks like a notation slip.
accuracy-def: Weighing models by accuracy section, p.2: 'Model accuracy a_theta is defined here as the proportion of correct classifications on the training set'.
rejection-sampling-def: Dequantising section, p.2: the authors explain rejection sampling (easy proposal q, scaling factor G with p <= Gq, accept if u'Gq < p). It is a standard textbook procedure that the paper defines for its own use.
not-all-schemes-dequantisable: Dequantising section, p.3: the authors state their dequantisation does not rule out a high-dimensional dataset where the scheme succeeds, and that other weighing schemes may not translate to a classical algorithm efficiently. This caveat limits the scope of their own result.
dj-embedding-conditions: Linking section, p.3-4: the embedding is an explicit construction (W uniform weights, A given by the stated gate product) checked step by step, DJ steps i-v against ensemble steps 1-5. It is a construction check, not a numbered theorem. Coordinator may reconsider.
dj-embedding-empty-data: Linking section, step 1, p.4: n equals the parameter bit length and the data register is assumed empty. These are stated conditions of the construction.
dj-embedding-hadamard-uncomputed: Linking section, steps 3-4, p.4: the extra Hadamards are stated to incorporate the ensemble into the DJ framework and are undone in step 4. It is a stated step of the construction.
conclusion-open-problem: Conclusion, p.4: the authors state that finding a meaningful quantum ensemble for ML that uses this advantage is still open, after saying the DJ reduction is not necessarily useful for ML. This is a limit stated about their own work.
appx-a-accuracy-def: Appendix A, Eq. 7, p.5-6: accuracy is defined explicitly, as an average over data of half the absolute value of f plus f*. Value matches.
appx-a-data-setup: Appendix A, p.6: inputs are standard-normal entries, l2 normalised, labels set by the sign of the first entry. Stated as the simulation setup.
appx-a-param-setup: Appendix A, p.6: parameters uniform on [-1,1], M = 10000 inputs and n = 100 parameter sets, stated as the simulation setup.
appx-a-simple-models-scope: Appendix A, p.6: the authors state they use base models with simple data to give an indication of viability. This sets the scope of the analysis.
appx-a-rates-vary: Appendix A, p.6: the authors state that for more realistic data the convergence rate may differ from the i.i.d. Gaussian case they analyse, and that rates must be estimated case by case. This caveat limits their own analysis.
appx-a-tractable-not-useful: Appendix A, p.6: 'This, however, does not say anything about whether the accuracy-weighted q-ensemble ... is a useful method'. It is a caveat on their own tractability finding.
appx-a-not-all-high-dim: Appendix A, p.7: after the poor test accuracy (0.50167) the authors state it does not imply poor performance on all high-dimensional datasets. This is a caveat on their own result. The cluster remark is hedged and cited.
appx-b-setup: Appendix B, p.8: the perceptron is a thresholding of X theta, and the ground truth theta* = [1,0,...,0] is chosen for simplicity (any uniformly sampled theta would do). Stated setup of the derivation.
abbas-dj-reduction-not-useful-ml: Conclusion, p.4: 'This Deutsch-Jozsa reduction, however, does not necessarily represent a quantum ensemble that is useful for machine learning.' It is a limit the authors state about their own result. The stored anchor says p.5, the text is on p.4.
abbas-ensemble-contains-deutsch-jozsa: Abstract, p.1 and Linking section, pp.3-4: containment is shown by an explicit construction checked step by step, DJ steps i-v against ensemble steps 1-5. It is not a numbered theorem, so this is the weakest form of 'proved'. The clause that DJ gives a speedup is the known cited property, with the deterministic-classical caveat.
qrc-atom-cavity-model-isolated: Section 2, p.3: two-level atom in a cavity, model 'entirely isolated from external influences', with only measurement-controlled interaction with a coherent input and cavity decay. This is the paper's stated model idealisation.
qrc-hamiltonians: Section 2-2.1, Eqs. 1-4: H_i = g a^dag a sigma- sigma+, H_c = -i beta (a^dag - a), H_z = g_z (sigma+ + sigma-), and H as their sum. Value matches.
qrc-stochastic-master-equation-simulatio: Section 2.1, Eq. 5, p.4: the dynamics use a stochastic master equation for a qubit and a cavity mode, collapse operator sqrt(kappa) a, and numerical solution of Eq. 5. Stated computational method.
qrc-input-encoding-and-optical-readout: Section 3, p.5: input data modulate the driving amplitude beta(t), information is carried by radiation delivered through one mirror, and detection is at the opposite side. Stated operating scheme.
qrc-linear-readout-pseudoinverse: Section 3, Eqs. 7-9, p.6: weights W = Y_train F^dagger(U_train) with the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, applied as Y_test = W F(U_test). Stated training protocol.
qrc-rmse-definition: Section 3, Eq. 10, p.6-7: RMSE over N points, normalised by the range y_max - y_min. Value matches.
qrc-accuracy-definition-epsilon: Section 3, Eq. 11, p.7: accuracy is the percentage of predictions within epsilon = 10^-2 of the target. Value matches.
qrc-classification-task-setup: Section 4.1, Fig. 4, p.7-8: synthetic sinusoidal and square waveform, output 0 for square and 1 for sinusoidal, data split into train and test, target not given at exploitation. Stated protocol.
qrc-mgts-task-setup: Section 4.2, Eq. 12, p.10: Mackey-Glass series with tau = 17, q = 10, beta = 0.2, gamma = 0.1 (the text spells it 'Mackay'), split into training and testing. Stated task setup.
qrc-generative-mode-setup: Section 4.2, p.10: free-running forecast with u_{n+1} = y_n, deliberately chosen because the authors say it is harder than the predictive mode. The choice and its reason are stated protocol, not a result.
qrc-damped-oscillator-task-setup: Section 4.3, p.12: the reservoir is shown several periods of a damped harmonic oscillator and must learn both frequency and amplitude. Stated task description.
qrc-further-analysis-deferred: Section 4.1, p.9: 'Further analysis of the physical properties of the reservoir and their impact on its computational performance will be reported elsewhere.' The paper states what it does not cover.
qrc-code-available-on-request: Data Availability Statement, p.14: the code is available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. It is the paper's own statement about what it provides.
qrc-validation-is-theoretical: Abstract, Introduction and Conclusions: the authors say they 'theoretically validate' the reservoir, and the whole paper is simulation with no hardware. It is the paper's own statement of its scope.

theory_low.abbas-gamma-scaling-vanishing-bound: Section 3.3, footnotes 10 and 11, p.5-6: both are one-line asides with no proof. Footnote 11 gives the scaling 'gamma ~ 32 pi alpha M^2/(d B^2)' using the unproved fact d_gamma,n <= d + tau/|log n|. Footnote 10 asserts c_{d,0} = 2 sqrt(d) with no derivation.
theory_low.abbas-remark-b3-relative-entropy-scaling: Appendix B.1, Remark B.3: the improved bound is claimed 'by following the proof above', with the log-Lipschitz property of relative entropy stated in a footnote as fact and the scaling of the inverse of t|log t| asserted. No separate proof is given.
theory_low.abbas-remark-b4-boundedness-relaxation: Appendix B.1, Remark B.4: 'one may be able to relax' is speculation about a possible extension. It is neither a proved result nor a stated failure of the paper's work, and the value says the same.
theory_low.abbas-barren-plateau-derivation-fisher-t: Section 3.4, p.6-7: the trace bound uses a barren-plateau definition taken from [23] (cited). The step from small trace to 'a spectrum concentrating near zero' and the converse 'unlikely to experience a barren plateau' are informal inferences, not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.dequantised-is-rejection-sampling: Dequantising section, p.2-3: an informal correspondence argument ('It turns out that ... may be translated'), not a theorem or lemma. The scheme is stated with an extra assumption elsewhere (point-symmetric parameter space) and the appendix shows both versions turn intractable in high dimension.
theory_low.postselection-mirrors-rejection: Dequantising section, p.3: 'If we associate Q with q(x) and P with p(x) then the postselection step mirrors the rejection decision' is an informal analogy with no stated conditions. It is not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.acceptance-probabilities-equal: Dequantising section, p.3: the equality is shown by a short inline comparison with the scale factor G left unspecified, no theorem statement and no conditions. The text layer also garbles the formulas. It is an informal derivation.
theory_low.dequantised-equals-measurements: Dequantising section, p.3: 'This directly corresponds to measurements obtained by the accuracy-weighted q-ensemble routine' is an authors' claim following the analogy. It is not proved as a statement.
theory_low.dequantise-high-dim-issues: Dequantising section, p.3: the first half is a cited field fact [21-23]. The second half rests on Appendix A simulations on simple data, a measured result and an authors' interpretation.
theory_low.dj-embedding-g-role: Linking section, p.4: 'g may now be thought of as a combination of ...' is an interpretive remark, not a result.
theory_low.dj-embedding-prediction-prob: Linking section, step 5, p.4: the paper writes p(f=0) as a weight sum over E+ and says it corresponds to prediction -1, while E+ was defined as the models predicting +1. The labelling is inconsistent in the paper, and the value repeats it, so the passage does not settle the pairing.
theory_low.dj-embedding-congruence: Linking section, p.4: 'demonstrated that the q-ensemble contains a classically hard computation amenable to a quantum advantage' rests on DJ being classically hard, a cited property [16,25] that holds for deterministic classical algorithms only. The conclusion itself says the reduction is not necessarily useful for ML. It is an authors' claim.
theory_low.dj-open-useful-routine: Linking section, p.4: 'opens doors for further research' is the authors' outlook, not a stated limitation of their results.
theory_low.conclusion-dequantise-and-study: Conclusion, p.4: 'show that a proposed implementation may be efficiently dequantised' restates the informal dequantisation argument, which has no theorem and which Appendix A qualifies. It is an authors' claim.
theory_low.appx-a-intractability-condition: Appendix A, p.5: the statement that both classical and quantum versions become intractable if accuracies tend to 0.5 with exponentially vanishing variance is a prose argument ('exponentially more precision will be required') with no theorem or proof.
theory_low.appx-a-mean-std-claim: Appendix A, p.6: for perceptron and linear models it points to an Appendix B derivation that is heuristic (law of large numbers, 'approximately equal' occurrence, limits taken inside expectations). For three-layer networks it says only 'numerical simulations suggest'. No theorem with conditions.
theory_low.appx-b-mean-half: Appendix B, Table I and Eqs. 9-10, p.7-8: the mean of 0.5 is argued from symmetry, 'approximately equal occurrence' and the law of large numbers, then 'confirmed by the simulated results'. It is a heuristic argument, not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.appx-b-variance-zero: Appendix B, Eq. 11 and after, p.8: the variance limit of 0 is obtained by taking d to infinity inside expectations with dropped terms, and 'holds for any uniformly sampled ground truth' is asserted. It is an informal derivation.
theory_low.abbas-accuracy-weighted-dequantised: Abstract, p.1 and Dequantising section, pp.2-3: 'can be fully dequantised' is stronger than the body. The argument is an informal rejection-sampling analogy with no theorem. The paper adds that other schemes may not dequantise, and Appendix A shows both versions turn intractable when accuracy variance vanishes exponentially. The passage does not prove full dequantisation.
